questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is not dangerous.
Can cause permanent hearing damage.
Is just a normal part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. This will protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use turn signals.
Use proper lane positions.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, signal your moves, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and stay ready to react.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Are not a concern.
Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if your motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular habit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if available. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Severely limits your vision.
Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit vision. It allows riders to see as much as they need for safe riding.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
Is always acceptable.
May affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter and prescription drugs, have side effects that can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication might affect your riding.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.
Stare at pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
questions.explanation: When looking for hazards, focus on finding escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: When wearing a helmet during a crash, a rider is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: All keep safe following distances.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: All keep safe following distances.
questions.explanation: Group riders should use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between each rider.

questions.question: Unlike other drinks, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into the bloodstream right away.
Must be digested.
Does not affect people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, they should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Look ahead at the road to help you avoid sudden stops.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle respond more slowly to your actions. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. When carrying a passenger, reduce your speed, start slowing down earlier, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: Poor braking:

options.text: Usually causes no problems.
Is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Poor braking is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Using proper braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up to higher gears.
Need to shift down to lower gears.
Need to put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up to higher gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Fit snugly.
Be uncomfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but they should not be so tight that they limit your movements.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Look straight ahead only.
Not be willing to move to avoid danger.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds to scan the path ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds to scan the path ahead.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on your path of travel. Looking ahead gives you time to react to danger before you reach it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will enter the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pay attention only to what is in front of you.
Pay attention only to what is behind you.
Pay attention to what is in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to what is in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: It is most important to watch the road ahead. However, you must also watch what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Usually not allowed.
Encouraged when traffic is heavy.
Okay if vehicles are moving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not allowed.
questions.explanation: Both cars and motorcycles need a full lane width to operate safely. For this reason, lane sharing is usually not allowed.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to help other drivers see you. This is important even during the day. Reflective clothing is also helpful.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Bright clothing to help others see you.
Any color clothing because drivers can see you easily in daylight.
Dark clothing to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing to help others see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Always wear bright colors to make yourself more visible when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road marks:

options.text: No parking allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows where the right edge of a traffic lane is.
